occurrences.text: ## Build inside your licensed SDK host

occurrences.text:
Set CAN_SDP_ENV to your trusted qnxsdp-env.sh, CAN_BUILD_FILE to your own working
SLM/libcan image buildfile, CAN_BSP_CWD to its working directory, CAN_OUT to a new
external build directory. The image must already contain slogger2, slog2info,
slm, slmctl, dev-can-linux, candump, cansend, and slm-can-fallback.xml, and emit
CANOPY_SLM_IMAGE_READY after startup. These are prerequisites, not shipped SDK
assets. Run:

reuse an old receipt for a new build. Stock SDK image construction may need the

occurrences.text: ## Collect on your Linux QEMU host
occurrences.historical_source_binding: UNVERIFIED unless exact declared field in referenced evidence; no commit inferred

occurrences.text:
Requires existing can-utils, QEMU kvaser_pci and your preconfigured isolated vcan
interface (host transport only). Use a single shared lease for SDK and target.
Stop/reap the SDK VM first. Collector checks effective host CPU <=100%, memory
<=1GiB and nice>=15; target stays 1vCPU/512MiB. A user-scope example:
occurrences.historical_source_binding: UNVERIFIED unless exact declared field in referenced evidence; no commit inferred

occurrences.text:
systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=100% -p MemoryMax=1G nice -n 15 \
      python3 tools/collect_native_incident.py --image "$CAN_OUT/incident.ifs" \
      --disk "$CAN_DISK" --out "$CAN_CAPTURE" --lock "$CAN_NATIVE_LOCK" \
      --interface "$CAN_INTERFACE"
occurrences.historical_source_binding: UNVERIFIED unless exact declared field in referenced evidence; no commit inferred

occurrences.text:
Choose a nonexistent capture directory. The collector refuses ambiguous identities,
starts actual SLM, invokes the separate native recorder against dev-can-linux,
observes replacement, and compares 100 ordered RX and 100 ordered TX frames using
independent host capture. It additionally invokes the actual threaded negative
control and snapshots slog2. All failures/raw serial/traffic remain; no retries
rewrite a prior incident. The narrow QEMU Kvaser PIRQ routing adjustment is recorded;
not a hardware BSP portability result. No safety/heartbeat/actuation/C6 work.

measurement. Traffic encoding is decimal ID + ':' + 16 lowercase hex bytes + newline,
preserving order; both complete streams are embedded and independently hashed.

occurrences.text: Root fields: schema (canopy.incident/2), collector, run, bindings, artifacts, events, seal.
occurrences.historical_source_binding: UNVERIFIED unless exact declared field in referenced evidence; no commit inferred

occurrences.text:
- collector: id, version, mechanism (IDs). Mechanism is descriptive, never selected or executed by importer. No slog2/secpol/dual-versus-in-process mechanism assumption.
- run: unique id; environment HOST_SIMULATION, RECORDED_QNX or FRESH_QNX; capturedAt/expiresAt date strings. Maximum 30-day window; capture at most 5 minutes in future. Expired input UNKNOWN. Labels are collector declarations, NOT independent QNX proof. Known synthetic/native collector contradictions and HOST descriptors relabelled native fail UNKNOWN; this does not detect a producer who forges all compatible declarations. FRESH_QNX denotes a newly collected bounded run, never a live connection.
- bindings: source, binary, image, disk: four distinct artifact paths with corresponding roles.
- artifacts: 1–32 records, each path, role, runId, text, sha256 (text digest), subjectSha256 (digest of underlying source set, executable, image, disk or raw observation stream). Roles source/binary/image/disk/observation. Native text receipts must record subject-digest computation, source revision + dirty content digest, build invocation/receipt linked input hashes, image/disk lineage and boot/run identity. Actual SDK/binaries/images/disks are NOT embedded. Importer checks text integrity and digest format, NOT native provenance. Host fixture descriptors explicitly are not real binaries/images.
- events: 1–2048 records: id, seq (zero-based consecutive), at (monotonic relative milliseconds, <=1 day), runId, kind, process, observer, evidence, data.
- process: name, positive integer pid, generation, domain. Other fields IDs. PID reuse is not a generation. Same generation must retain identical identity. Domain identifies a boundary, not proof of security enforcement.
- observer: name, generation, independent boolean. Self-generation cannot claim independence. Independence is collector provenance, not attestation. Native receipts must identify actual separate observer and collection channel.
- evidence: 1–8 path/line objects pointing to embedded observation text (1-based). Displayed escaped, never fetched/executed.
- data by kind (closed fields):
  - process/interruption/recovery: state observed or absent.
  - kill: signal SIGKILL; actual target/result, not intended command.
  - traffic: direction RX or TX, count exactly 100, positive bytes <=1 MiB, expectedSha256, observedSha256, ordered boolean. Adapter defines canonical ordered frame encoding in evidence and preserves expected/actual streams or derivation. Independent observer must actually compare 100 frames each direction. Importer compares digests, not unavailable hardware.
  - control: mode in_process, outcome cofailure_observed or not_observed; members (exactly two distinct named members, each name/process/before/after), trigger, termination, survivor (before/after event IDs). Both members must carry the exact control process identity including PID/generation/domain and distinct observed-before/absent-after process event IDs. The SIGKILL trigger and independently observed process termination must match that identity, be ordered after member-before observations and before member-after observations. The separate survivor must retain exact identity, differ in PID/generation/domain, and have independent before/after observations around that control fault. All referenced events precede the summary. Process-wide termination can establish both member absences; do not invent per-thread telemetry. Missing/ambiguous/mismatched bindings invalidate the pack to UNKNOWN.
  - optional ssh: session, phase before/after, challenge, responseSha256. After requires same session, later event and distinct challenge. Emit only actual same-session challenges, never serial or reconnect disguised as SSH. V2 displays evidence but offers NO SSH continuity verdict or authenticated session proof.

occurrences.text: Limits: 2 MiB input, nesting <24, 128 Ki characters/artifact, 1 MiB total artifact UTF-8, 32 artifacts, 2048 events, 8 references/event, paths <=180 characters. occurrences.text: ## Historical host-only two-layer model (not native safety)
occurrences.historical_source_binding: UNVERIFIED unless exact declared field in referenced evidence; no commit inferred

occurrences.text:
- Classic CAN ID 0x200, four bytes: state, brake percentage, low-nibble
  alive counter (upper nibble must be zero), CRC. CRC-8/SAE-J1850
  (poly 0x1d, init/xorout 0xff, no reflection) covers ID bytes 02 00 then
  state/brake/counter. Known-answer check: 123456789 -> 0x4b.
  E2E-style detection only; **not AUTOSAR conformance or authentication**.
- Actuator independently asserts 100% brake and hazards at >=100 ms since
  last accepted frame. Constant model deceleration is 4 m/s² at full brake;
  this is an illustrative controlled-stop model, not validated vehicle physics.
  Integration splits at the timeout even if the next scheduler call is late.
- Bad CRC, malformed fields, wrong ID, frozen, backward and skipped counters
  never refresh that deadline. Exact +1 modulo 16 is required while active.
  Timeout recovery requires ten consecutive SAFE_STOP frames with fresh counters;
  the first may establish a new counter baseline but cannot repeat the last one.
  DRIVE cannot re-arm a timed-out actuator. Restart and wrap ambiguity remains:
  a four-bit counter is not replay protection against an adversary.
- Safestop starts latched. Signal ages >30 ms, obstacle <=5 m, nonfinite values,
  pilot request outside 0..20 m/s, or cycle gap >20 ms latch stop. These are
  **application model parameters**, not measurements or validated limits.
  Only ten fresh healthy cycles release the latch. Cycle ten still emits full
  SAFE_STOP for actuator synchronization; subsequent fresh cycles reduce brake
  by 10 percentage points per cycle. Pilot has no latch-clear API.
- Pure model tests run in one process. The [live host runtime](docs/host-runtime.md)
  separately schedules the actuator and sender on Linux vcan; exact owned-child
  SIGSTOP/SIGKILL tests verify independent timeout behavior. This is not a QNX
  driver-kill, microkernel isolation, scheduling guarantee or physical watchdog.
